profile.reading: This record is named Cyxtera Tampa TP1 in this registry, mapped to Tampa, Florida. No corporate website could be reached for this operator this session, and no independent secondary source describing this specific facility was found, so address, capacity, and square footage remain not published in this record. Cyxtera Technologies, headquartered in Coral Gables, Florida, entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement with Brookfield Infrastructure, disclosed via an SEC Form 8-K titled "Cyxtera x Brookfield APA Press Release" and filed November 2, 2023, per SEC EDGAR's full-text search index; this registry has not independently confirmed the full scope of that transaction (whether it covered Cyxtera's entire US colocation portfolio or a subset) beyond the filing's existence. Separately, Cologix, a different operator tracked elsewhere in this registry, acquired two specific Cyxtera facilities, VAN5 in Vancouver and MTL12 in Montreal, in 2023, per Cologix's own materials; those two Canadian facilities are unrelated to this Florida facility and to the Brookfield transaction. Cyxtera's own public website resolves but displays content that reads as dated (referencing a 2017 executive appointment) with no current facility locations list, and its data-centers subpage returns a certificate error, a combination consistent with a company mid-transition following the Brookfield transaction rather than one actively maintaining public marketing infrastructure. No square footage, MW capacity, or current operational status specific to this Tampa facility was located in sourcing reachable this session. Fresh research this session, using web search tools unavailable in the prior exhausted pass, confirms this reverse geocoded address as the TPA1-A building, a 99,000 square foot facility with 6.3 megawatts of combined leased and available IT capacity per DataCenterHawk. Cyxtera itself filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in June 2023 after operating more than 60 facilities totaling over 245 megawatts across 29 global markets; Brookfield Infrastructure Partners and institutional partners agreed to acquire seven of Cyxteras US data centers for 775 million dollars, including this Tampa property, in a deal that closed in early 2024 and merged Cyxteras retained facilities with Brookfields existing Evoque colocation platform into a combined operator later rebranded Centersquare, with over 330 megawatts of combined North American capacity.

reading.body:
Cyxtera Tampa TP1 is a 99,000 square foot facility in Hillsborough County with 6.3 megawatts of published IT capacity. The facility was acquired by Brookfield Infrastructure in early 2024 as part of a $775 million acquisition of seven Cyxtera US data centers, following Cyxtera's Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing in June 2023. Brookfield subsequently merged Cyxtera's retained assets with its existing Evoque colocation platform into a combined operator rebranded as Centersquare.

At typical AI training densities of 40 kilowatts per rack, this 6.3 megawatts of IT load translates to roughly 155 racks as an assumption. The facility's specifications do not disclose what certifications or architectural features it holds, or what workload classes it qualifies to host.

Within Florida's published data center inventory, this campus ranks fifth by megawatt capacity among the four facilities that disclose power figures in the state. Florida's total published capacity across 13 mapped facilities stands at 9.35 megawatts, meaning this single site represents 67 percent of the state's disclosed IT load. The operator's web presence remains dated and fragmented, consistent with post-acquisition integration rather than active independent marketing, and no current public visibility exists for Cyxtera's facilities list or operational status.
